name: עֻזִּיָּהוּ
summary: Above all Uzziah son of Amaziah, king of Judah for fifty-two years (2Ch 26:1–3), also called Azariah (2Ki 15:1); in his days Isaiah, Hosea and Amos prophesied, and there was the earthquake Zechariah recalls (Isa 1:1; Hos 1:1; Amo 1:1; Zec 14:5). He was helped by God “until he was strong; but when he was strong his heart was lifted up”, and burning incense in the temple he was struck with leprosy until the day of his death (2Ch 26:15–21); in the year he died Isaiah saw Yahweh's glory (Isa 6:1). He is in the genealogy of Jesus (Mat 1:8–9, Ὀζίας). The name is also borne by a Kohathite Levite (1Ch 6:9), the father of Jonathan over David's treasuries (1Ch 27:25), a priest of the sons of Harim (Ezr 10:21), a man of Judah (Neh 11:4), and, spelled עֻזִּיָּא, Uzzia the Ashterathite among David's mighty men (1Ch 11:44). The name is עֻזִּי “my strength” with יָהוּ: the words of Israel's song, “my strength (עָזִּי) and my song is Yah” (Exo 15:2).

evidence.note: “All the people of Judah took עֻזִּיָּהוּ, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.”
Spelled עֻזִיָּה; the same king is עֲזַרְיָה in 2Ki 15:1.
“When he was strong (וּכְחֶזְקָתוֹ) his heart was lifted up to destruction, and he trespassed against Yahweh his God.”
“Uzziah the king was a leper until the day of his death.”
“In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up.”
“As you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah.”
Ὀζίας in the genealogy of Jesus Christ.
A Kohathite: “Uriel his son, Uzziah his son, Shaul his son.”
“Jonathan son of Uzziah” over the treasuries in the field.
Of the sons of Harim, among those with foreign wives.
“Athaiah son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah”, of Judah, in Jerusalem.
“עֻזִיָּא the Ashterathite”, among David's mighty men.
“עָזִּי and my song is Yah”: the name's two parts together.

note: Takes p.bx.am (עֻזִּיָּהוּ, עֻזִּיָּה; 27 tokens) and p.bx.an (עֻזִּיָּא, 1Ch 11:44, one token). TIPNR's Uzziah@1Ch.6.24 is 1Ch 6:9 in the Hebrew numbering. The king's other name עֲזַרְיָה (Azariah, “Yahweh has helped”) is of the root עזר and is not claimed. The reading “Yahweh is my strength” takes עֻזִּי as עֹז with “my”, as in Exo 15:2 and Psa 28:7; scripture does not explain the name. Phoenician names of the same shape (ʿzbʿl “Baal is my bulwark”) are the cognate evidence.
